question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the normal line to the polar curve $r=4\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4},$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta )=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+4\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ), \\ {x}^{′}(\theta )=2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-4\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

The Cartesian equation of the normal line is $y=$
{{field-1}} $x\,+$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the normal line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+4\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-4\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+4\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-4\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})+4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})}{2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})-4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{2}{2-\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\pi \cdot {(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2} \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =4\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the normal:

We find the equation of the normal as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{m}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\frac{\pi }{2} & =\frac{\pi -2}{2}(x-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ y & =\frac{\pi -2}{2}\,x+\frac{\pi (4-\pi )}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
